Biodiversity accross a fiber treatment

Roger Calvas

2025-04-14

Goals

Run an analysis on the within-sample biodiversity of the samples in our project.

  1. Calculate the Hill Numbers of the samples using the iNEXT package.
  2. Plot and evaluate the interpolated and extrapolated rarefaction curves from iNEXT.
  3. Analyze the Hill numbers as it relates to status and short chain fatty acids concenctrations in milimoles per kilogram.
  4. Test and then answer the scientific question at hand! (Remember, we’re doing biology!)

Inputs

  1. We will need the phytree_preprocessed_physeq, which includes a rooted tree (ideally within the archaea!) that we created in analysis/04B_Phylogenetic_Tree_Inspection.Rmd.

Outputs

This is an exciting analysis!!! We finally get to answer one of our scientific questions!

  1. Calculated biodiversity measures (Hill numbers) across every sample.
  2. Figures to include in our scientific paper that visualize the data as it relates to the scientific question.
  3. Statistical tests conveying the measured and quantified changes and patterns in biodiversity.

Scientific Question

Question & Hypotheses

How is microbial diversity and short chain fatty acid concentrations (scfa) modified by inulin treatment.

  • Null Hypothesis: Microbial diversity and scfa production does not vary during inulin treatment
  • Alternative Hypothesis: Microbial diversity and scfa production will increase during an inulin treatment. Establishing a correlation between fermentable fiber and gut biota.

Set up the Environment

Timing of this script

# What time did we start running this script? 
start_time <- Sys.time()

Set the seed

set.seed(3980)

Load Packages & Colors

# install packages for stats
#install.packages("rstatix")
#install.packages("ggpubr")

pacman::p_load(tidyverse, devtools, patchwork, iNEXT, phyloseq,
               # packages for stats
               ggpubr, rstatix, install = FALSE)

# Load in colors for plotting 
source("code/colors.R")

  theme(legend.position = "none") + 
  labs(y = "Effective Number of ASVs", x = "Number of Sequences")

##   .. ..$ qD.LCL    : num [1:9177] 0.981 83.724 95.955 101.912 105.479 ...
##   .. ..$ qD.UCL    : num [1:9177] 1.02 87.12 99.7 105.88 109.58 ...
##  $ AsyEst  :'data.frame':    483 obs. of  7 variables:
##   ..$ Assemblage: chr [1:483] "SRR6443836" "SRR6443836" "SRR6443836" "SRR6443839" ...
##   ..$ Diversity : chr [1:483] "Species richness" "Shannon diversity" "Simpson diversity" "Species richness" ...
##   ..$ Observed  : num [1:483] 116 33.1 18.2 236 83.6 ...
##   ..$ Estimator : num [1:483] 116 33.2 18.2 236 84 ...
##   ..$ s.e.      : num [1:483] 1.987 0.293 0.216 2.033 0.591 ...
##   ..$ LCL       : num [1:483] 116 32.7 17.8 236 82.8 ...
##   ..$ UCL       : num [1:483] 119.9 33.8 18.7 240 85.1 ...
##  - attr(*, "class")= chr "iNEXT"
iNEXT_manual_df <- 
  iNEXT_data$iNextEst$size_based %>%
  dplyr::rename(names = Assemblage) %>%
  # join with the metadata
  left_join(., metadata_df, by = "names") %>%
  mutate(status = factor(status, levels = c("before",
                                              "during")))

# Inspection
dim(iNEXT_manual_df)
## [1] 19320    63
# Manually plot rarefaction curves 
iNEXT_manual_df %>%
  # Filter out rows that are calculated with actual sequences (no extrapolated)
  dplyr::filter(Method == "Rarefaction") %>%
  # Now, let's draw the plot! 
  ggplot(aes(x = m, y = qD, color = status, group = names)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  # Facet by status 
  facet_grid(Order.q~status, scales = "free") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = status_colors) + 
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(y = "Effective Number of ASVs", x = "Number of Sequences") + 
  theme(legend.position = "none")

#Interpretation 1: Sequencing depth is likely sufficient, all curves plateau even in richness. There is an outlier sample during the treatment that has an unusually high amount of ASVs, I will need to be in the lookout for that.

Run Shapiro-Wilk for the scf

shapiro.test(metadata_df$Butyrate)

shapiro.test(metadata_df$acetate)

shapiro.test(metadata_df$propionate)

shapiro.test(metadata_df$total_scfa)

Now richness is not normal, so we need to use non parametric tests.

Kruskal wallis for the different scf

# Calculate the kruskall-wallis stats
kw_status_butyrate <- 
  obs_whole_rich_df %>%
  kruskal_test(Butyrate ~ status) 

# Look at it 
kw_status_butyrate

Statistically test Richness

# Pull out richness data 
obs_rich_df <- 
  obs_div_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(Order.q == 0)

kw_status_rich <- 
  obs_rich_df %>%
  kruskal_test(qD ~ status)

# View results
kw_status_rich
## # A tibble: 1 × 6
##   .y.       n statistic    df     p method        
## * <chr> <int>     <dbl> <int> <dbl> <chr>         
## 1 qD      161      2.23     1 0.135 Kruskal-Wallis
summary(kw_status_rich)
##      .y.                  n         statistic           df          p        
##  Length:1           Min.   :161   Min.   :2.229   Min.   :1   Min.   :0.135  
##  Class :character   1st Qu.:161   1st Qu.:2.229   1st Qu.:1   1st Qu.:0.135  
##  Mode  :character   Median :161   Median :2.229   Median :1   Median :0.135  
##                     Mean   :161   Mean   :2.229   Mean   :1   Mean   :0.135  
##                     3rd Qu.:161   3rd Qu.:2.229   3rd Qu.:1   3rd Qu.:0.135  
##                     Max.   :161   Max.   :2.229   Max.   :1   Max.   :0.135  
##     method         
##  Length:1          
##  Class :character  
##  Mode  :character  
##                    
##                    
## 
rich_ggboxplot <-
  ggboxplot(obs_rich_df, x = "status", y = "qD", fill = "status", 
             color = "status", alpha = 0.3,
          outlier.shape = NA) + 
 geom_jitter(aes(color = status)) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = status_colors) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = status_colors) + 
  labs(y = "# of Total ASVs (Richness)") + 
  stat_compare_means(method = "kruskal.test", label.y = min(obs_rich_df$qD)) + 
  geom_pwc(
    aes(group = status), tip.length = 0, hide.ns = TRUE,
    method = "t_test", label = "p.adj.format",
    p.adjust.method = "fdr", bracket.nudge.y = -0.08) + 
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30,
                                   hjust = 1, 
                                   vjust = 1))
# Pull out simpson data 
obs_simpson_df <- 
  obs_div_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(Order.q == 2)
# Kruskal walis test
kw_simpson_df <- 
  obs_rich_df %>%
  kruskal_test(qD ~ status)

# View results
kw_simpson_df

# Show the plots
rich_ggboxplot + simpson_ggboxplot

#Interpretation 2: I can conclude based on the kruskal-wallis tests that rare taxa change based on the inulin treatment but dominant taxa stay relatively stable with a non-significant change. #Interpretation 3: The kruskall-wallis test is testing for a difference in microbial composition before and after the inulin treatment, a significant value in richness means that rare taxa are affected by a dietary intervention with fermentable fibers, although dominant species maintain stable.

``` r

obs_div_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = total_scfa, y = qD)) + 
  facet_wrap(.~Order.q, scales = "free") + 
  geom_point(aes(color = status)) +

There appears to be a negative relationship between scfa concentration and effective number of ASVs in the common and dominant, while the richness stays stable ( mainly in the extrapolations the actual data does not reflect clear trends)

#Spearman correlation

```{r-spearman-correl}

richness_df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = total_scfa, y = qD)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = status)) + 
  stat_smooth(method = "lm") + 
  labs(x = "total SCFA", y = "# of ASVs") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = status_colors) + 
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_blank()) + 
  stat_cor(method = "spearman", label.x = 3, label.y = 30)

#Interpretation 4: Richness and rare taxa were the only ones that changed statistically significantly but it looks like total_scfa is not able to significantly explain this change, so scfa production does not relate to changes in richness significantly.

#Interpretation 5: I checked it by asking if total_scfa could explain the changes in richness observed during the kruskall wallis test, because a part of my scientific question was to determine whether scfa concentrations changed with diversity after the inulin treatment.
